tools.name: list_strings
tools.title: List Strings
tools.description: List every provider-reported string object or candidate, or filter to one address, as address/value pairs with encoding, terminator status, and byte length when available. Hopper reads complete typed objects and retains its original display text as provider_value; long literals may span adjacent unterminated objects. Kuna scans mapped printable sequences of at least five characters, including unterminated fragments; references are not computed. Select detail summary for counts and retained native-inventory pages; complete remains the default.

tools.name: read_function_instructions
tools.title: Read Function Instructions
tools.description: Return every raw instruction for one analyzed procedure. Instruction text and body extent are provider-specific. Ghidra terminal-call assumptions that may cut the analyzed body are reported in limitations.

tools.name: search_bytes
tools.title: Search Bytes
tools.description: Find masked byte signatures in initialized analyzed memory. Hex byte pairs and ?? wildcards are supported; an optional equal-length hex mask selects bits. Bounds are inclusive. Matches are ordered by provider address and never span blocks. Coverage describes this page; reuse the same query with next_cursor to continue. Uninitialized blocks are listed separately. Ghidra only; Hopper is unavailable.

tools.name: read_bytes
tools.title: Read Bytes
tools.description: Read analyzed bytes from one provider-normalized virtual address. The hexadecimal payload reports the exact returned length; incomplete reads remain explicit and unsupported provider APIs return typed capability unavailability.

tools.name: search_strings
tools.title: Search Strings
tools.description: Search every provider-reported string object or candidate using literal matching by default or regex when requested. Results are deterministic and complete over that provider inventory, not every text sequence in artifact bytes. Kuna scans mapped sequences of at least five characters, including unterminated fragments, without computing references. Ghidra may omit packed or undefined literals, including Rust strings; an empty result does not prove text is absent. If an address is known, read_bytes and xrefs inspect its bytes and references. Hopper retains typed byte decoding, native display, and explicit decoding unknowns. Adjacent long-literal fragments match independently. Hopper regex mode uses ECMAScript Unicode syntax in a cancellable worker. The matching deadline is REA_REGEX_MATCHING_DEADLINE_MS (a positive decimal integer of milliseconds from 1 to 2147483647, default 5000). Unset keeps the default. A deadline failure names the effective milliseconds, source (default or setting), the default, and the maximum, and leaves the API usable. The worker old-generation request is REA_REGEX_WORKER_HEAP_REQUEST_MIB (a decimal integer of mebibytes from 7 to 16384, default 128). Unset keeps the default. A positive Node --max-old-space-size, including NODE_OPTIONS, overrides that request and is not limited by the setting's floor or maximum. A heap failure names the effective request, its source (default or setting), the default, the floor, and the maximum. Select detail summary for counts and retained native-inventory pages; complete remains the default.

tools.name: xrefs
tools.title: Xrefs
tools.description: Return analyzed references to a code or data address. Hopper may default to its current cursor; headless providers such as Ghidra require an explicit address. Use to connect strings, globals, selectors, and functions; bare addresses are untyped and indirect references may be incomplete. Use inspect_native_instruction at the target address for typed incoming references where supported.

tools.name: find_xrefs_to_name
tools.title: Find Xrefs To Name
tools.description: Resolve an exact name against the bound provider's name inventory and return a resolved or unresolved result. Unresolved names use the stable name_not_found reason; this xref workflow returns address-only projections.

tools.name: analyze_function
tools.title: Analyze Function
tools.description: Build a dossier for one native function identified by symbol or provider-returned address. Returns identity with complete inclusive analyzed body ranges or explicit unknown, provider-specific pseudocode and assembly, comments, calls, references, referenced strings/names, local CFG blocks, and available native API boundary observations. Ghidra terminal-call assumptions that may cut the analyzed body are reported in limitations with available callee identities. Default detail summary returns a compact dossier (identity, pseudocode size, facet counts, value-flow availability) and retains the complete dossier Evidence in this session; page pseudocode, references, assembly and value-flow through normalized_result.parent_evidence_id with inspect_analysis_view. detail complete returns the full dossier inline.

tools.name: open_binary
tools.title: Open Binary
tools.description: Open a local executable, application bundle, archive, JavaScript, source map, plist, or analysis database after validation. format=dos-com explicitly interprets 1..65280 headerless bytes as a DOS COM analysis image. format=raw-binary interprets headerless bytes with a required architecture and entry_point; file offset 0 maps at that address. Omission preserves header-based detection. provider_id selects one deep provider or deterministic auto selection; the binding remains stable until close or an explicit switch, with no failure fallback. Reopening the same target and profile retains its active database and metadata edits. An optional analysis snapshot is imported atomically and must match the binary identity, concrete provider, and canonical analysis profile exactly; importing into a session with metadata mutations requires closing and reopening it first. Call close_binary when the investigation is finished.

path.description: Absolute local filesystem path for the analysis target; relative paths are rejected.

format.description: Explicit interpretation: dos-com or raw-binary (headerless), or gamecube-dol (GameCube/Wii DOL, never auto-detected). Omission preserves header-based detection.

architecture.description: Caller-supplied CPU family. Required with format=raw-binary; rejected otherwise. format=gamecube-dol takes powerpc from the header, so it must be omitted.

entry_point.description: Caller-supplied load and entry address (0xhex). File offset 0 is mapped here. Required with format=raw-binary; rejected otherwise. Optional with format=gamecube-dol; must equal the DOL header entry.

provider_id.description: Exact deep-analysis provider ID, or automatic selection when omitted.

snapshot_path.description: Absolute local filesystem path for the analysis snapshot; relative paths are rejected.

inputSchema.description: Advertised in reduced form by the compact input schema profile; the server still validates complete canonical inputs.
